q1_issues.issue: (On bam silk_road) asserts a locative relation that no word licenses — 'Silk Road city' contains no preposition — so the head is world knowledge added as content, not an oblique named after its own preposition.
'hacked ... for survivors' names what was being searched for, not a party the hacking is done for the benefit of, so it belongs in the preposition-named For oblique rather than Beneficiary.
A group of survivors is asserted to exist, although 'hacked through debris for survivors' entails no survivors.

'international' is predicated of the group symbol, the reading the plural rules warn against, since a descriptive modifier on a plural distributes to the members unless it is genuinely a property of the collection.
Both plurals are grouped and both predicates are distributive (hack, overflow), yet neither group gets the per-member distribution rule the grouped-plural rule requires alongside the group event.

q2_gaps: a proper-noun modifier inside a nominal ('Silk Road city') — the compound-concept rules explicitly exclude proper nouns and give no way to attach the named modifier to the head noun

a bare-plural subject of a specific past episode ('International rescue workers hacked ... yesterday') — bare plurals route to generic rules and definite/counted plurals to group witnesses, leaving the episodic bare plural unaddressed
notes: The compound genus (rescue_worker/worker with the noun modifier unexposed), the participial modifier 'flattened' kept in adjective form, the Through oblique, the Manner adverb, and the geography (LocatedIn bam iran, Member bam city, Member bam ancient) all follow the instruction set. The head On is a licensed form in general — the objection is that this sentence supplies no preposition for it.
